transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because... I just spend most of my day going back over the same outlets, and the locks, and, well, my tools. And the dust. I just keep checking them and fixing them again and again until I'm just completely worn out. And even then, I still don't feel sure enough to just leave it alone. 

It’s funny I mention the dust, actually, because my neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she has this dog—a Golden Retriever, I think—and it sheds everywhere. I mean, everywhere. She let him out the other day, and the wind just blew a whole tumbleweed of hair right onto my porch. I was trying to sweep it up, but the broom I have is one of those cheap plastic ones, you know? The bristles get all bent out of shape if you press too hard. I bought it at that hardware store down on 4th Street, the one that used to be a diner. They had the best cherry pie there when I was a kid. But anyway, yeah, I just... I can't stop checking things around the house. It's exhausting.
Do you feel like you have to check these things in a specific way or order?

Well, yeah, like I was saying, it's always the same things, so I guess there is an order to it. I'll start with the outlets, then the locks, then my tools, and then the dust. I just spend most of my day going back over those exact same things in that loop. I check them, and I fix them, again and again until I'm just completely worn out. But even when I'm exhausted, I still don't feel sure enough to actually leave it alone. 

Take my tools, for example. I have to make sure they're perfectly set in the garage. My uncle actually gave me my first real socket set. He was a mechanic over at the old dealership on Route 9. They tore that place down a few years ago to build a strip mall, which is a real shame because they had this huge, vintage neon sign out front. It buzzed really loud at night, you know? Kinda sounded like a swarm of bees. I got stung by a bee once when I was ten, right on the eyelid. Swelled up like a baseball, I couldn't see out of it for three days. My mom had to put this weird baking soda paste on it. 

But anyway, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the order. Yeah, I just keep going through the outlets and the locks and everything else all day until I'm dead on my feet, but it never feels like it's done right.
Are you checking these things because you're afraid something bad will happen if you don't?

Yeah, it's... that's exactly it. Even when I know, logically, that I did the job right, these ugly thoughts just keep jumping in. Like, I'll convince myself that a loose wire I missed is going to spark and burn the whole house down. Fire is just... it's terrifying. I actually saw a house burn down when I was a teenager. It was the Miller family, two streets over. The fire trucks came, and they actually had one of those Dalmatian dogs riding in the front seat. You don't really see that much anymore, do you? I watched this program on TV about Dalmatians once, and apparently they're actually pretty high-strung dogs. Not like in that cartoon movie at all. My wife loves those old cartoons, she actually collects the vintage VHS tapes in those big plastic clamshell cases. They take up a whole bookshelf in the living room. 

But... where was I? Oh, right, the bad things. Yeah, or I'll think about a nail I might have left somewhere on the garage floor, and I just picture my wife stepping on it and getting really hurt. I try so hard to push the thoughts out, I just squeeze my eyes shut and try to force them away, but they come right back stronger. And if she stepped on a rusty nail, she'd have to go get a tetanus shot. I hate needles. The last time I got a shot, the nurse bruised my arm so bad it was purple and yellow for a week. I had to wear long sleeves in the middle of July, and it was sweltering that year. The AC in my truck was broken, too, so I was just sweating through my flannel every time I drove anywhere. 

But yeah, I just... I check because I can't stop those thoughts about the house burning or her getting hurt. They just won't leave me alone.

Do these thoughts about something bad happening, like the house burning down or your wife getting hurt, feel like they're coming from outside of your own thinking, or are they more like your own worries?

Outside of my own thinking? I... I don't really know what you mean by that. Like, like someone else is broadcasting them into my head? I don't know if I'd say that, but I'm not really sure how to describe it either. I haven't really noticed if they feel like 'mine' or not, they're just... there. 

But you know, mentioning broadcasting, my granddad actually used to have this massive HAM radio setup out in his shed. He was really into all that stuff, used to bounce signals off the atmosphere and talk to people all the way in Australia. Can you imagine? Just sitting in a dusty shed and talking to a guy in Sydney. I always wanted to go to Australia, but the flights are, what, like twenty hours long? I can't sit still for that long. Plus, the seats on airplanes nowadays are so small. My knees always get jammed up against the tray table. The last time I flew anywhere was down to Florida for my cousin's wedding, and the guy in front of me reclined his seat the whole way. Spilled half my ginger ale right on my lap. It was sticky for the whole flight, and the ice melted into my jeans. 

But, uh... wait. What were we talking about? My worries? Yeah, I just... I don't really know how to answer that one. They just won't stop, wherever they come from.
Do these thoughts about bad things happening feel like they are forcing their way into your mind, or are they more like thoughts you're having because you're worried?

Yeah, I guess like I was saying before, they definitely force their way in. Even when I know for an absolute fact that I did the job perfectly right, these ugly thoughts just keep jumping into my head anyway. Like the loose wire burning the house down, or the nail I left on the floor hurting my wife. I try so hard to push them out, but they just come right back stronger. 

It's kind of like trying to hold a beach ball underwater. Have you ever tried doing that? We used to go to this community pool when I was a kid, over on Elm Street. The lifeguard there was this older guy named Gary, always had a whistle on this bright red lanyard. He'd blow that whistle at us if we were dunking each other or running. One time my brother swallowed a bunch of pool water and threw up right on the concrete deck. They had to close the whole place down for the afternoon and pour this weird smelling powder all over it. It smelled like strong bleach and mint. I actually can't stand the smell of mint anymore because of that. Even peppermint gum makes my stomach turn. My wife chews that wintergreen stuff sometimes, and I always have to ask her to roll the window down if we're in the car. Her car has those automatic windows, but the button on the passenger side sticks, so you have to press it really hard... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, if the thoughts force their way in. Yeah, they just jump right in and take over, and I can't push them away no matter how hard I try.
Do you feel like these thoughts about bad things happening are a part of your own thinking, or do they feel alien to you?

Alien? I... I don't really know. Like I was trying to say earlier, I haven't really thought about it like that. I don't know if they're my own or if they feel alien, they're just... they're just always in my head. 

When you say alien, though, it makes me think of my neighbor, Mr. Henderson. He's got this massive telescope set up on his back deck. He's always out there at two in the morning looking at the stars. I know because I'm usually up getting a glass of water or something, and I can see him through the kitchen window. He swears he saw a UFO hovering over the town water tower last month. You know that water tower on Route 9? They just repainted it last summer. It used to be this faded baby blue, but now it's bright white with the town logo on it. But the guys who painted it messed up the stencil, so the 'R' in the town name looks like a 'P'. My buddy Dave works for the public works department, and he said it's going to cost them like five grand to get a crew back up there to fix one letter. Five grand! Can you believe how expensive everything is getting? I went to the hardware store to buy a sheet of plywood the other day and... 

Wait, sorry. Alien thoughts. Right. Um, yeah, I really couldn't tell you. I just haven't noticed if they feel like they belong to me or not.
When these thoughts about bad things happening come into your mind, do you feel like they're something you want to think about or something that's being imposed on you?

No, I definitely don't want to think about them. It's like I was saying, they just impose themselves on me. Even when I know for a fact, like, absolutely 100% sure that I did a job completely right, these ugly thoughts just keep jumping into my head anyway. Like that a loose wire I missed is going to spark and burn the whole house down, or a nail I dropped is going to get stepped on and hurt my wife. I try so hard to push them out, but they just come right back stronger. 

Speaking of nails, I actually buy mine in bulk from this old hardware store downtown. Not one of those big box places, you know? It's called Miller's, and the floorboards in there creak so loud when you walk down the aisles. Old man Miller still runs the register, and he uses one of those ancient mechanical ones where you have to punch the keys down really hard and it goes *ding* when the drawer pops open. He always gives me a piece of butterscotch candy when I check out. I don't really like butterscotch, it gets stuck in my teeth, but I take it anyway to be polite. I usually just leave it in the center console of my truck. I think there's probably a dozen of them melting together in there right now. The sun beats down on my driveway all afternoon, and the inside of the cab gets like an oven. I need to get one of those reflective sunshades, the ones that fold up like an accordion. My dad had one with a picture of sunglasses on it...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask? If I want to think about them? No, definitely not. They just force their way in and I can't stop them.
When you have these thoughts about bad things happening, do you feel like they're a part of who you are or do they feel like they're not really yours?

I mean, it's kind of like what I was just saying before. I really couldn't tell you if they feel like they're mine or not. I've never really stopped to think about whether they're a part of who I am, I just know they won't go away. 

When you say "part of who I am," though, it actually reminds me of when I was filling out all that paperwork to renew my driver's license last week. I had to go down to the DMV on 4th Street. You know the one next to that old bowling alley? The bowling alley is totally boarded up now. It's a real shame, I used to go there for cosmic bowling all the time when I was in high school. They had these blacklights everywhere and this crazy neon carpet with little stars and planets glowing on it. My buddy Steve actually slipped on that carpet once because he wore his bowling shoes all the way over to the snack bar. You're really not supposed to do that, it completely ruins the slide on the sole of the shoe. Anyway, he slipped and dropped a whole tray of nachos. Fake cheese just went everywhere, all over the carpet. The guy working the shoe counter got so mad, his face turned bright red. 

Steve actually moved down to Florida a couple years ago. Tampa, I think? Or maybe Orlando. Somewhere with a lot of golf courses. He sells boats now, which is funny because he used to get terribly seasick when we were kids...

Wait, sorry, I lost track again. What did you ask me? If the thoughts are a part of me? Yeah, I just... I really don't know. I can't tell.
When you have these thoughts about bad things happening, do you feel like they are in line with your own values and beliefs?

Values and beliefs? Uh... I don't know, honestly. I've never really thought about it like that. I don't think I have any values about houses burning down or people getting hurt on nails. I mean, nobody wants that, right? 

Speaking of values, though, it makes me think of my grandpa. He was always talking about the value of a hard day's work. He used to work at the old textile mill over in the next county. That whole place is shut down now, they turned it into those fancy loft apartments with the exposed brick walls. I looked at renting one of those when I first moved out of my parents' house, but they wanted, like, two thousand a month for a studio. A studio! You're basically sleeping in your kitchen. And the parking was terrible. You had to park on the street, and there's this one street sweeper that comes by every Tuesday morning at 5 AM. It's the loudest thing I've ever heard, sounds like a jet engine driving down the road. 

My buddy Mark lived in a place like that for a while, and his car got towed three times because he kept forgetting to move it for the street sweeper. It was a 1998 Honda Civic, the thing was basically held together by duct tape and hope. He ended up just selling it to a junkyard for three hundred bucks and bought a bicycle. But then someone stole the front tire off his bike while he was at the grocery store...

Sorry, what was the question? My values? Yeah, I don't know. The thoughts are just there, I don't know if they match up with anything I believe.
Do you feel like these thoughts about bad things happening are in conflict with the kind of person you think you are?

Conflict with the kind of person I am? I... I don't really know. I've never really sat down and thought about what kind of person I am compared to the thoughts. I just try to get through the day, you know? 

Getting through the day, man, that reminds me of when I was working that overnight security gig a few years back. It was at this huge warehouse out by the interstate, the one where they store all those bulk paper towels and toilet paper. You wouldn't believe how much toilet paper a city goes through. Anyway, the night shift was brutal. From midnight to 8 AM, just walking the perimeter. The worst part was the vending machine in the breakroom. It was one of those old ones with the coils, and it was completely unpredictable. I put a dollar in once for a bag of those jalapeño chips—the ones in the green bag, you know?—and the coil turned, but the chips just got stuck right at the edge. Just dangling there. I tried shaking the machine, which you're not supposed to do, but I was so hungry. The security guard before me, this guy named Gary, told me if you hit the side of it right next to the coin return, it sometimes knocks things loose. Gary was a character. He always wore these clip-on ties because he said a real tie was a choking hazard if someone broke in. Like anyone's breaking into a paper towel warehouse to strangle the security guard, right? 

He actually got fired because he fell asleep in the golf cart we used to patrol the back lot. Drove it straight into a stack of pallets. The pallets were fine, but the cart's bumper was completely cracked...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. What did you ask me? If the thoughts conflict with who I am? I honestly have no idea. I just know they're there all the time.
Do you feel like these thoughts about bad things happening are something you'd normally think about, or do they seem out of character for you?

Out of character? Um... I couldn't really tell you. I've been having them so much that I don't even know what my normal character is supposed to be anymore. Like, what is normal, right? 

Speaking of normal, that makes me think of my neighbor, Mrs. Higgins. She's anything but normal. She has this routine where she comes out every single morning at exactly 6:15 to water her plastic flamingos. I'm not kidding, she takes a little green watering can and waters the plastic birds on her front lawn. She's got about twelve of them out there. One time, the wind blew really hard during a storm and knocked three of them over, and she was out there at midnight with a flashlight, staking them back into the mud. 

That storm was crazy, actually. It knocked the power out for two whole days on our block. I had to empty my entire fridge because everything went bad. All my milk, my eggs, this giant tub of potato salad I'd just bought from the deli down the street. The guy at the deli, Frank, makes the best potato salad. He puts a little bit of dill in it, which sounds weird, but it totally works. Frank's been running that place for twenty years. He's got this huge collection of vintage baseball caps hanging on the wall behind the counter. He told me once he got an original Brooklyn Dodgers hat at a garage sale for fifty cents. Can you believe that? Fifty cents! He said the guy selling it didn't know what he had. Frank put it in a glass case by the register, right next to the lottery tickets. I bought a scratch-off from him once and won five bucks, which I just used to buy a turkey sandwich...

Oh, man. Sorry. I'm completely off track again, aren't I? What were we talking about? Oh, if the thoughts are out of character. Yeah, I just... I really don't know what my normal character is. I couldn't say.

Do you feel like these thoughts about bad things happening are something that you would normally agree with or want to think about, or do they feel like they're contradicting your own desires or beliefs?

Agree with them? Or want to think about them? I mean... I don't know if I want much of anything these days. It's hard to even figure out what my desires are, honestly, so I don't know if the thoughts contradict them or not. 

Talking about desires, though, my brother was just asking me what I wanted for my birthday next month. He was looking at getting me one of those air fryers. Everyone's obsessed with air fryers right now, right? He got one for his wife last Christmas and she makes everything in it. Chicken wings, mozzarella sticks, even Brussels sprouts. I don't even like Brussels sprouts. When we were kids, my mom used to boil them until they were basically gray mush. The smell was awful, it would stink up the whole house for days. 

We lived in this tiny little ranch house back then, the kind with the really low ceilings and that ugly orange shag carpet. My dad spent a whole summer trying to rip that carpet up himself instead of hiring someone. He found these original hardwood floors underneath, but they were covered in this rock-hard black glue. He tried everything to get it off—scraping it, using this toxic-smelling chemical stripper he bought at the hardware store. The fumes were so bad we had to sleep at my aunt's house for three nights. My aunt had these two huge golden retrievers that shed everywhere. You couldn't sit on the couch without getting covered in blonde hair. She used to vacuum twice a day with this massive old Hoover that sounded like a lawnmower...

Uh... sorry. I lost my train of thought again. What were you saying about desires? Yeah, I really couldn't tell you if the thoughts contradict anything. I just don't know.
Do you feel like these thoughts about bad things happening are something that you would normally think, or do they feel foreign to your own way of thinking?

Foreign to my way of thinking? I... I don't know if I can even say what my way of thinking is anymore. It's just a jumble up there. I really couldn't tell you if they feel foreign or not. 

Foreign... that reminds me of this guy I met at the laundromat last week. He was from somewhere in Eastern Europe, I think. He was trying to figure out the coin machine, but it was one of those digital ones that takes a card, not quarters. I tried to help him, but neither of us could get the stupid app to download on our phones because the service in that building is terrible. It's in the basement of this old brick apartment complex. 

The super there, this guy named Mike, is always walking around with a giant ring of keys. Like, fifty keys on one carabiner. He jingles everywhere he goes. You can hear him coming from three floors away. Mike's actually a pretty good guy, though. He helped me jump my car battery a couple of months ago when it died in the parking lot. It was freezing cold, like ten degrees out, and my heater core was broken anyway, so I was driving around with blankets on my lap. I finally took it to this mechanic, Sal, down on 4th Street. Sal's garage is amazing, it's packed to the ceiling with old hubcaps. He collects them. He's got hubcaps from cars they haven't made since the seventies. He was showing me this one from a Ford Pinto...

Wait. Oh, geez. I did it again, didn't I? I'm sorry. You were asking about my thoughts? If they feel foreign? Yeah, I just... I really don't know. I'm just not sure.
Do you feel like these thoughts about bad things happening are in line with how you see yourself as a person?

In line with how I see myself? I don't... I don't even know how I see myself as a person anymore. I mean, what does that even mean, really? I'm just so overwhelmed all the time, I couldn't tell you if they line up with who I am or not. 

Seeing myself... you know, I was actually looking at myself in the mirror this morning, trying to decide if I should shave my beard. I've had it for like, three years now. I started growing it when I got laid off from my last job at the warehouse. They shut the whole place down, moved the operations out of state. It was a huge place, too, like a million square feet. We used to drive these little golf carts around inside just to get from one end to the other. 

The guy who drove the cart most of the time was this older dude, Gary. Gary was obsessed with fishing. Every Monday, he'd come in and tell us about whatever he caught over the weekend at the lake. He had this massive tackle box that he actually brought into the break room once to show me. It had like a hundred different lures in it, all these crazy neon colors. He said the neon green ones worked best for bass. He even offered to take me out on his boat sometime, this little aluminum dinghy he bought off Craigslist. He said the guy he bought it from threw in a free trolling motor, but the motor was missing a propeller, so Gary had to order a replacement part from some website in China. It took like two months to arrive, and when it finally did, the box was completely crushed...

Oh, man. I'm doing it again. I am so sorry. My brain just won't stay put. You were asking about how I see myself? Yeah, I just... I really don't know the answer to that. I couldn't say.
Do you feel like these thoughts about bad things happening are something that you would normally think, or do they feel like they are not coming from you?

Coming from me? I mean, I guess they have to be coming from me because they're in my head, right? But they don't feel like *me*. Like... I used to do a lot of handyman stuff around the house, right? And even when I know I did the job right, these ugly thoughts keep jumping in that a loose wire I missed is going to burn the house down, or a nail I left somewhere is going to hurt my wife. I try to push them out, but they come right back stronger. 

It's like that time I tried to fix the garbage disposal. My wife, she loves to cook, but she puts everything down that drain. Potato peels, coffee grounds, you name it. One day it just made this horrible grinding noise and stopped working. So I got under the sink with my flashlight. It's so cramped down there, and it smelled like old onions. I found this little plastic dinosaur jammed in the blades. It was one of those cheap toys you get out of a quarter machine at the grocery store. The grocery store down the street from us, they have a whole row of those machines. They used to have one that dispensed those sticky hands you throw at the wall. I loved those when I was a kid. But they leave this greasy residue on the paint. My mom got so mad at me once because I threw one at the ceiling and it got stuck there for like a week. When it finally fell down, there was this perfect hand-shaped stain on the popcorn ceiling...

Oh, shoot. I'm sorry. I drifted off again, didn't I? But yeah, about the thoughts... I try to push them away, but they just keep coming back. It's exhausting.
Do you feel like these thoughts about bad things happening are something that you would personally agree with or find acceptable?

Agree with them? I... honestly, I don't even know what's acceptable anymore. I couldn't really give you a straight answer on if I agree with them or not. Everything's just so loud in my head.

Acceptable... that's actually the exact word the insurance adjuster used last year when he came to look at our roof. We had this crazy hailstorm, right? The hail was the size of golf balls. It dented the hood of my neighbor's truck so bad it looked like a golf ball itself. He drives this vintage Chevy, cherry red. He spends every Sunday out there waxing it in his driveway. He uses this special imported wax from Germany that he orders online. He let me smell it once, and it smelled exactly like bananas. Which is super weird for car wax, you know? 

It actually made me crave banana bread. My grandma used to make the best banana bread when I was a kid. She'd put walnuts in it, but only on one half because my grandpa was allergic to nuts. He'd break out in hives if he even looked at a walnut. He had to carry one of those EpiPens everywhere he went. He actually left it at a diner once, and we had to drive all the way back across town in rush hour traffic to get it. The traffic was bumper to bumper because someone had dropped a whole mattress in the middle of the highway. Just a bare mattress, right in the fast lane. People were swerving everywhere to avoid it, and this one guy in a minivan...

Ah, crap. I'm doing it again. I am so sorry, my mind just completely wandered off on me. You were asking if the thoughts are acceptable to me? Yeah, I just... I don't know. I really couldn't say.
Do you feel like these thoughts about bad things happening are something that you would typically think, or do they seem out of place with your own thoughts and beliefs?

Out of place? I... I don't know. Maybe? It's hard to tell what's typically me anymore, you know? I just can't really say if they fit or not. 

Out of place... like, that reminds me of when we went to this fancy restaurant for our anniversary last month. I felt totally out of place there. They had three different forks at every seat. Who needs three forks? The waiter was wearing a literal tuxedo, and he kept coming over to scrape crumbs off the table with this little metal tool. It looked like a tiny snow shovel. 

Speaking of snow, we haven't had a decent snowfall here in like five years. I used to love shoveling the driveway when I was a teenager. I'd do the neighbors' driveways too for ten bucks a pop. I saved up enough one winter to buy a used PlayStation. The guy I bought it from lived in this apartment complex where all the doors were painted bright yellow. It was blinding. He had this massive iguana just walking around his living room like a dog. He fed it lettuce right out of his hand. He said he got it from a reptile expo down in Florida. My aunt lives in Florida, actually. She moved there after she retired from the post office. She was a mail carrier for thirty years and has the craziest stories about dogs chasing her. She actually got bit once by a tiny Pomeranian...

Oh, man. I'm so sorry. I completely lost track again. You asked if the thoughts seem out of place? Yeah, I just... I really don't know the answer to that. I'm not sure.
Do you feel like these thoughts about bad things happening are something that you would personally consider to be 'you' or a part of your own identity?

Part of my identity? I mean... I don't think so. Like I was saying earlier about the handyman stuff, you know? I'll finish a job, and I know for a fact I did it right, but then those ugly thoughts just force their way in anyway. The ones about missing a loose wire that's gonna spark and burn the house to the ground, or dropping a nail that my wife is going to step on and get seriously hurt. I try so hard to push them out of my head, but they just come back stronger. That doesn't feel like *my* identity. 

Speaking of identity, though... my buddy Mark actually had his identity stolen a couple of years ago. It was a total nightmare. Somebody got his information and bought, like, three jet skis down in Miami. He had to spend months on the phone with the bank trying to sort it out. He was always on hold, listening to that terrible elevator music. You know the kind, with the really cheesy smooth jazz saxophone? My uncle used to play the saxophone. He was actually in a jazz band in the eighties. They played at weddings mostly, and he wore this powder blue suit to every single gig. It had these massive shoulder pads. He looked like a football player trying to play a woodwind instrument. He actually did play football in high school, but he blew out his knee during a scrimmage. He slipped on a patch of mud and just... popped. He had to wear this huge metal brace for a year. It squeaked every time he walked down the hallway...

Ugh, man, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I am so sorry. My brain just will not stay on track today. But yeah, to answer your question... no, those thoughts about the fires and the nails and stuff, I don't consider them to be 'me'. I just can't seem to stop them.

doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Compulsions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because I spend most of my day going back over the same outlets, locks, tools, and dust in the house, checking and fixing them again and again until I’m worn out and still don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone.
target_item.reason: This is the first turn of the consultation, so I must return my chief complaint symptom code, which is S066.

patient.answer:
Well, I’m here because... I just spend most of my day going back over the same outlets, and the locks, and, well, my tools. And the dust. I just keep checking them and fixing them again and again until I'm just completely worn out. And even then, I still don't feel sure enough to just leave it alone. 

It’s funny I mention the dust, actually, because my neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she has this dog—a Golden Retriever, I think—and it sheds everywhere. I mean, everywhere. She let him out the other day, and the wind just blew a whole tumbleweed of hair right onto my porch. I was trying to sweep it up, but the broom I have is one of those cheap plastic ones, you know? The bristles get all bent out of shape if you press too hard. I bought it at that hardware store down on 4th Street, the one that used to be a diner. They had the best cherry pie there when I was a kid. But anyway, yeah, I just... I can't stop checking things around the house. It's exhausting.

doctor.intent: determine presence of compulsions to perform specific rituals
doctor.question: Do you feel like you have to check these things in a specific way or order?

target_item.name: Compulsions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because I spend most of my day going back over the same outlets, locks, tools, and dust in the house, checking and fixing them again and again until I’m worn out and still don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the specifics of the checking behavior (compulsions), specifically if they must be performed in a specific way or order, which aligns with the description of compulsions.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, like I was saying, it's always the same things, so I guess there is an order to it. I'll start with the outlets, then the locks, then my tools, and then the dust. I just spend most of my day going back over those exact same things in that loop. I check them, and I fix them, again and again until I'm just completely worn out. But even when I'm exhausted, I still don't feel sure enough to actually leave it alone. 

Take my tools, for example. I have to make sure they're perfectly set in the garage. My uncle actually gave me my first real socket set. He was a mechanic over at the old dealership on Route 9. Out of place? I... I don't know. Maybe? It's hard to tell what's typically me anymore, you know? I just can't really say if they fit or not. 

Out of place... like, that reminds me of when we went to this fancy restaurant for our anniversary last month. I felt totally out of place there. They had three different forks at every seat. Who needs three forks? The waiter was wearing a literal tuxedo, and he kept coming over to scrape crumbs off the table with this little metal tool. It looked like a tiny snow shovel. 

Speaking of snow, we haven't had a decent snowfall here in like five years. I used to love shoveling the driveway when I was a teenager. I'd do the neighbors' driveways too for ten bucks a pop. I saved up enough one winter to buy a used PlayStation. The guy I bought it from lived in this apartment complex where all the doors were painted bright yellow. It was blinding. He had this massive iguana just walking around his living room like a dog. He fed it lettuce right out of his hand. He said he got it from a reptile expo down in Florida. My aunt lives in Florida, actually. She moved there after she retired from the post office. She was a mail carrier for thirty years and has the craziest stories about dogs chasing her. She actually got bit once by a tiny Pomeranian...

Oh, man. I'm so sorry. I completely lost track again. You asked if the thoughts seem out of place? Yeah, I just... I really don't know the answer to that. I'm not sure.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's thoughts are ego-dystonic
doctor.question: Do you feel like these thoughts about bad things happening are something that you would personally consider to be 'you' or a part of your own identity?

target_item.name: Obsessions
target_item.manifestation: Even when I know I did the job right, these ugly thoughts keep jumping in that a loose wire I missed is going to burn the house down or a nail I left somewhere is going to hurt my wife, and I try to push them out but they come right back stronger.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the nature of the patient's thoughts ('Do you feel like these thoughts about bad things happening are something that you would personally consider to be 'you' or a part of your own identity?'), which is exploring the ego-dystonic nature of the obsessions.

patient.answer:
Part of my identity? I mean... I don't think so. Like I was saying earlier about the handyman stuff, you know? I'll finish a job, and I know for a fact I did it right, but then those ugly thoughts just force their way in anyway. The ones about missing a loose wire that's gonna spark and burn the house to the ground, or dropping a nail that my wife is going to step on and get seriously hurt. I try so hard to push them out of my head, but they just come back stronger. That doesn't feel like *my* identity. 

Speaking of identity, though... my buddy Mark actually had his identity stolen a couple of years ago. It was a total nightmare. Somebody got his information and bought, like, three jet skis down in Miami. He had to spend months on the phone with the bank trying to sort it out. He was always on hold, listening to that terrible elevator music. You know the kind, with the really cheesy smooth jazz saxophone? My uncle used to play the saxophone. He was actually in a jazz band in the eighties. They played at weddings mostly, and he wore this powder blue suit to every single gig. It had these massive shoulder pads. He looked like a football player trying to play a woodwind instrument. He actually did play football in high school, but he blew out his knee during a scrimmage. He slipped on a patch of mud and just... popped. He had to wear this huge metal brace for a year. It squeaked every time he walked down the hallway...

Ugh, man, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I am so sorry. My brain just will not stay on track today. But yeah, to answer your question... no, those thoughts about the fires and the nails and stuff, I don't consider them to be 'me'. I just can't seem to stop them.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of recurrent, intrusive thoughts about bad things happening, such as the house burning down or his wife getting hurt, and his compulsions to check things repeatedly, are characteristic of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). The patient's difficulty in controlling these thoughts and his significant distress and impairment in daily life also support this diagnosis.
